## PM callback registration

In `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`, the PM operations register:

```c
.suspend       = i915_pm_suspend,
.suspend_late  = i915_pm_suspend_late,
.suspend_noirq = i915_pm_suspend_noirq,
.poweroff      = i915_pm_suspend,
```

The tree does **not** contain a function named `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`; runtime suspend is implemented as `intel_runtime_suspend()`.

## Call chains reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

There are two PM-operation entries that invoke the same callback:

### System suspend

```text
PCI/device PM core
  └─ i915_pm_ops.suspend
       └─ i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
            ├─ i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
            ├─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
            │    └─ ...
            └─ i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)
                 └─ ...
```

### Hibernation poweroff

```text
PCI/device PM core
  └─ i915_pm_ops.poweroff
       └─ i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
            ├─ i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
            ├─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
            │    └─ ...
            └─ i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)
                 └─ ...
```

Thus, `.suspend` and `.poweroff` are the two PM callbacks reaching `i915_pm_suspend`; they share the same complete call chain.

The other system-PM callbacks do not call `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
.suspend_late   └─ i915_pm_suspend_late()
.suspend_noirq  └─ i915_pm_suspend_noirq()
.freeze         └─ i915_pm_freeze()
.freeze_late    └─ i915_pm_freeze_late()
```

## Callers that also call runtime suspend

None.

The requested symbol `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` is absent from `drivers/gpu/drm/i915`. The runtime callback is instead:

```text
PCI/device PM core
  └─ i915_pm_ops.runtime_suspend
       └─ intel_runtime_suspend(struct device *kdev)
            ├─ dev_priv = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
            ├─ i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
            ├─ intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
            └─ intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt)
```

Therefore neither caller of `i915_pm_suspend`—the `.suspend` path nor the `.poweroff` path—also calls the runtime-suspend callback.

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The display portion of `i915_drm_suspend()` is:

```text
i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
  └─ i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
            └─ dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
                 └─ display = dev_priv->display
                      └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

The relevant object conversions and field flow are:

```text
struct device *kdev
  └─ kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       └─ struct drm_i915_private *i915/dev_priv

struct drm_device *dev == &dev_priv->drm
  └─ to_i915(dev)
       └─ same struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv

dev_priv->display
  └─ struct intel_display *display
       └─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

The current tree names the final function `intel_display_driver_suspend()`, not `intel_display_suspend()`.
